Thought: I need to determine how the hydrolysis of oximes can be facilitated. Let me think about the chemistry of oximes and their hydrolysis reactions.

Oximes have the general structure R1R2C=NOH. Hydrolysis of oximes involves breaking the C=N bond to form a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) and hydroxylamine (NH2OH).

The hydrolysis of oximes typically requires catalysis, and acid catalysis is particularly effective for this reaction. In acidic conditions, the nitrogen atom of the oxime becomes protonated, making it a better leaving group and facilitating the addition of water to break the C=N bond.

So, heating in acidic solution would facilitate the hydrolysis of oximes. This corresponds to option A.
